title: Formal glueing: the module H^0 of a glueing datum localizes to its components
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $f_1,\dots,f_t\in R$. Let $\mathbf M=(M',(M_i)_i,(\alpha_i)_i,(\alpha_{ij})_{i,j})$ be an object of the category $\mathrm{Glue}(R\to S,f_1,\dots,f_t)$ of glueing data [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]: $M'$ an $S$-module, $M_i$ an $R_{f_i}$-module [def-weil-ring-localization-away], $\alpha_i:M'_{f_i}\to M_i\otimes_RS$ and $\alpha_{ij}:(M_i)_{f_j}\to(M_j)_{f_i}$ isomorphisms satisfying conditions (a) and (b) there; here $P_f$ is the localization of an $R$-module $P$ at $f$ with localization map $p\mapsto p/1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] and $P\otimes_RS$ the base change [def-weil-module-base-change]. Let $H^0(\mathbf M)$ be the $R$-submodule of $M'\times\prod_{i=1}^tM_i$ of the families $(m',(m_i)_i)$ with $\alpha_i(m'/1)=m_i\otimes1$ in $M_i\otimes_RS$ and $\alpha_{ij}(m_i/1)=m_j/1$ in $(M_j)_{f_i}$ for all $i,j$, and $p_i:H^0(\mathbf M)\to M_i$, $(m',(m_k)_k)\mapsto m_i$, the projection. Fix $i$. Then there is exactly one $R$-linear map $\pi_i:H^0(\mathbf M)_{f_i}\to M_i$ with $\pi_i(h/1)=p_i(h)$ for all $h\in H^0(\mathbf M)$, and $\pi_i$ is bijective.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence, line 24813), second paragraph: the morphism Psi from Can(H^0(M)) to M becomes an isomorphism after the base change R -> R' = R_{f_i}, by combining Lemma 05EQ (lemma-base-change-glue, line 24792; H^0 commutes with the flat base change R -> R_{f_i}) and Lemma 05EP (lemma-equivalence-I-unit, line 24768; the case (f_1,...,f_t) = R, proved with Algebra Lemma 00EQ, lemma-glue-modules, algebra.tex line 4439). Stated here is the i-th module component of that isomorphism; H^0 is defined in Remark 05EL (remark-glueing-data, line 24641).
